_what: A PROTOTYPE SEMANTIC PASS over this repository, WRITTEN BY THE RESEARCHER BY HAND on 2026-09-10. It is not the output of any agent, no agent CLI was launched and no token was spent. It exists so the checker beside it has something real to bound, and so the phase can report how much of a hand-written semantic description deterministic evidence can actually hold.
_method: Components, journeys and gates were written from READING the source, in the order a model with source access would: name the part by its job, say what it takes and gives, say where it runs, say what it keeps, say where it stops. Each claim then names the file:line the writer believed carried it. NOTHING was copied out of the fact base while writing; the citations are the writer's, and the checker's job is to say which of them the deterministic half can actually see.
_not_a_proposal: This is not a proposed schema for docs/arch/. Research 66's pinned key set and refusal 8 are untouched; a direction that needs them moved says so in the research document and leaves the decision to the operator.

components.name: Sessions that outlive the window
components.job: Keep a named terminal session alive across a quit, a crash and a reboot, in a tmux server the app does not own.
components.input: a project folder, an agent choice and a name
components.output: a live session the app can attach to and detach from without ending it
components.runsIn: the private tmux server, spoken to from main
components.state: the session itself, in tmux; nothing durable in the app
components.limit: the app is a disposable client, so nothing here survives the tmux server being killed by hand

facts.why: main starts a tmux probe as a child of its own
the identity stamp every managed pane carries
the list format that reads @gmux-id back

components.name: The record that makes restore possible
components.job: Remember every session's project, agent and resume argument so the app can put the world back after it is gone.
components.output: rows the restore pass reads at boot
components.runsIn: main, in a SQLite file under the app's data directory
components.state: sessions, projects, restore attempts, remote projects and remote executions
components.limit: a row can outlive the tmux session it names, which is why restore asks tmux rather than trusting the row

facts.why: a restore attempt is written down before it is tried

components.name: The pane you actually type into
components.job: Give a window a real terminal attached to one durable session, and take it away again without ending the session.
components.input: a session id and a size
components.runsIn: main, one pty per attached session
components.state: none of its own; the scrollback lives in tmux
components.limit: a pane's width is the window's, so a narrow window reflows the session's history

facts.why: the plan is pure and starts nothing

components.name: The picture of the folder you are in
components.job: Read a repository's tracked files and imports with no model and no turn, and draw what is made of what.
components.output: a partition, one sentence per box, and an import graph
components.runsIn: main, off one file watcher subscription, with a worker pool for parsing
components.state: a derived database that can be deleted without loss
components.limit: every edge it can draw is an import, so a system whose parts talk over HTTP or a socket shows no connection at all

facts.why: the picture is composed here and nowhere else

components.name: The one door that rewrites your file
components.job: Replace a file's bytes only when the bytes on disk are still the bytes the caller read.
components.input: a path, a payload and the digest of what was read
components.output: written, stale, raced, read-only or refused
components.runsIn: main, synchronously, so the stat, the read and the digest describe one moment
components.state: none; it stages beside the file and renames
components.limit: a change of the same size inside one timestamp tick is invisible, which on this filesystem is a nanosecond

facts.why: the whole channel is this one function
the read refuses to follow a link
the staged copy is created exclusively

components.name: What the agent changed, drawn over what you had
components.job: Show an agent's edit as a marking against a shadow copy of the file, and let a person take one change back or keep it.
components.input: the file on disk and the baseline the tab is holding
components.output: a drawn marking, and on a press either the file or the baseline rewritten
components.runsIn: the renderer, writing through the guarded door
components.state: the baseline, durable under the app's data directory
components.limit: losing the baseline store loses the narrowing and nothing on disk, because the file is the file and git is the history

facts.why: a press asks the generation guard before it reads

components.name: A folder on another machine, which feels like this one
components.job: Run the same session and file work against a machine reached over ssh, without the surfaces saying they are remote.
components.input: a confirmed machine and a folder on it
components.output: sessions, trees, diffs and searches that read the same as local ones
components.runsIn: main, through one exec plane that is the only place this product runs ssh
components.state: remote projects and remote executions in the manifest, and a bounded local mirror for the architecture read
components.limit: nothing Tortie writes runs on the machine beyond a fixed set of scripts, and the model slot stays local

facts.why: one of the two places ssh is run

components.name: Which account an agent signs in as
components.job: Let a person keep more than one vendor account and choose which one a session launches under, without a sign-in ever being performed by Tortie.
components.input: a provider and a chosen login
components.output: the environment a pane is launched with, and a credential kept for the account a store moved away from
components.runsIn: main, with the keychain and the vendor's own store directories
components.state: a login record, a scoped keychain item per login, and the vendor's own files
components.limit: the person's own default location is read-only forever except on a deliberate switch, and there is no refresh and no rotation

facts.why: the one delete, guarded by an ownership test
an exclusive create so a planted link cannot take the write

components.name: Opening a file a transcript named
components.job: Let a click on a path an agent printed open that file, without letting a click run a program.
components.input: a path span found in a terminal row
components.output: the file opened inside Tortie, or handed to the system for the one kind that is allowed
components.runsIn: main answers the door; the renderer only underlines
components.limit: between the answer and the open the file at that path can be replaced, so the allowlist is one extension wide

facts.why: the allowlist is asked after the mode check

journeys.name: Start an agent on a project, quit, and come back to it

steps.label: Tortie creates a session in the private tmux server and stamps it with an id of its own
the pane is launched under the login the person chose

facts.why: the pane environment is composed here

steps.label: the row is written before anything can be lost
a pty attaches so the person can type
after a reboot the restore pass reads the rows and asks tmux what is still there

journeys.name: An agent rewrites a file and you take one change back

steps.label: the watcher notices the file moved and the redline is drawn against the tab's baseline

facts.why: the press asks the generation guard

steps.label: a rewind rewrites the file only if the bytes on disk are still the bytes that were read
an accept moves the baseline instead and leaves the file alone

journeys.name: Open a folder on another machine and work in it

steps.label: the machine is confirmed once, out of band of any agent turn
the remote project is remembered so it comes back
the architecture read runs against a bounded mirror of that folder

gates.question: Tortie finds a session in the private tmux server. Will it adopt it?
gates.because: a session that carries neither an id option of ours nor the pane stamp is not ours, and is never adopted and never killed

facts.why: the id option is read on every list

gates.question: A configuration file names an agent binary. Will Tortie launch it?
gates.because: nothing starts on a configuration change alone; a person confirms the fields out of band and the agreement is bound to a hash of the fields that decide what runs

facts.why: the confirmed hash is the agreement

gates.question: You press save and the file changed on disk since Tortie read it. Will it be overwritten?
gates.because: the guarded door answers stale rather than writing, and the person is asked with Compare as the default

gates.question: A transcript prints a path to a .command file and you click it. Will it run?
gates.because: the mode is checked before the extension and the allowlist of kinds handed to the system is one extension wide

gates.question: The architecture check finds the contract has drifted. Will a model be started?
gates.because: only when an agent has been chosen in Settings, the confirm gate still holds at the spawn, the drift is real and the minimum interval has passed; otherwise nothing runs

gates.question: You choose a different login while a session of that provider is running. Will the store be written?
gates.because: it is written under the vendor's own locks, and a lock the vendor holds is a refusal naming the lock rather than a steal
